testPolicy.text: Brown requires SAT or ACT scores for first-year applicants (superscored; essay/writing optional; ACT Science optional since spring 2025). CDS C8F: required for all first-year students except first-year veterans applying via the veteran application.

gpa.doc: Brown does not publish an average GPA on the pages readable without a browser

cost.totalIncludes: Incoming first-year full-time student: tuition 74,568 + fees 3,084 (includes 100 academic record fee for first-time students) + housing 10,710 + food 8,754 (direct charges 97,116) + miscellaneous personal 2,878. Books are not a separate line (most scholarship students are in a book/course materials program); travel not included.

aidPromise.text: Need-blind admission and 100 percent of demonstrated need met; The Brown Promise eliminates packaged loans from all undergraduate aid offers (100% of aided students have no loans in their packages); $0 parent contribution for most families with less than $60,000 in annual income.

facts.text: For the Class of 2030 (fall 2026), Brown received 47,944 applications and admitted 2,687 (5.6%), 889 of them through Early Decision.
Brown admitted 889 students through binding Early Decision for the Class of 2030, about a third of the 2,687 admits.
The 2026-27 cost of attendance for an incoming first-year is $99,994, and The Brown Promise means no loans are packaged in aid offers.
Brown also runs two small combined programs with their own pools: Brown|RISD Dual Degree (856 applicants, 20 enrolled) and the eight-year medical program PLME (4,687 applicants, 50 enrolled).

notes: Brown publishes its CDS only as a Tableau dashboard (https://oir.brown.edu/institutional-data/common-data-set). The project forbids reading pages in a browser, and the Tableau CSV export only returns one worksheet per dashboard, so the CDS C section (fall 2025 counts, C9 enrolled scores, ED counts, residency, waitlist) is not used: cycle is null and the newest cycle comes from the admission office page (Class of 2030, fall 2026: 47,944 applications, 2,687 admitted, 1,723 first-year students, 889 admitted Early Decision). Scores are the Class of 2030 admitted-student middle 50% from the same page (admitted, not enrolled; 25th-75th only). The G-section values (housing 10,710, food 8,754, other 2,878) were cross-checked through the Tableau CSV export of G-Expenses, which curl can read. Brown's tuition-aid page also links 'New Student Tuition and Fees for the 2025-2026 Academic Year' but the finaid cost page gives 2026-27, which is used. I did not find on Brown pages a statement about need-aware treatment of international applicants or a $200,000 tuition-free tier, so neither is claimed. Accessed 2026-10-13.
